recipes.title: Classic Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Add chicken, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, broth, thyme and bay leaves to the pot.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure and remove the lid.
Take out chicken, shred with two forks, and return to the pot.
Turn on Sauté, add egg noodles, and simmer 6-8 minutes until tender.
Discard bay leaves, season with salt and pepper, and serve.
recipes.tip: Add the noodles after pressure cooking so they don't turn mushy.

recipes.title: Hearty Beef Stew
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and brown the beef in batches; set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic 2 minutes, then stir in tomato paste.
Add beef back with broth, Worcestershire, thyme, carrots and potatoes.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 35 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release the rest.
Turn on Sauté, stir in cornstarch slurry, and simmer 3-4 minutes until thickened. Season and serve.
recipes.tip: Browning the beef first builds deep flavor; don't skip it.

recipes.title: Classic Beef Chili
steps: Turn on Sauté and brown the ground beef; drain excess fat.
Add onion and garlic, cook 2 minutes, then stir in chili powder and cumin.
Add tomatoes, beans, broth and salt; stir well.
Seal lid and run Bean/Chili (or Pressure Cook High) for 20 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Stir and serve with desired toppings.
recipes.tip: Let it rest 10 minutes before serving so the flavors meld and it thickens.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Soup
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion, carrots and garlic 3 minutes.
Stir in cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add lentils and broth.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Stir in lemon juice, season, and blend partially if you prefer it smooth.
recipes.tip: Red lentils break down naturally, so no blending is needed for a creamy texture.

recipes.title: Italian Minestrone Soup
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion, carrots, celery and garlic 4 minutes.
Add tomatoes, beans, broth, herbs and pasta.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Stir in spinach until wilted, season, and serve with grated Parmesan.
recipes.tip: Use a sturdy small pasta like ditalini so it holds up under pressure.

recipes.title: Split Pea Soup with Ham
ingredients: 1 lb dried green split peas, rinsed
1 ham bone or 1.5 cups diced ham
steps: Add split peas, ham, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, broth and bay leaf to the pot.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 15 minutes.
Natural release 15 minutes, then quick release.
Discard bay leaf and ham bone; shred any meat back into the soup.
Stir, season, and serve.
recipes.tip: No soaking needed for split peas; a full natural release makes them extra creamy.

recipes.title: Creamy Tomato Soup
steps: Turn on Sauté, melt butter, and cook onion and garlic 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes, broth and sugar.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Blend smooth with an immersion blender, stir in cream and basil, and season.
recipes.tip: Add the cream after blending and off pressure to keep it from curdling.

recipes.title: Black Bean Soup
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion, pepper and garlic 4 minutes.
Stir in cumin and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add beans and broth.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 35 minutes.
Natural release 15 minutes, then quick release.
Blend partially for body, stir in lime juice, season with salt, and serve.
recipes.tip: Don't add salt before cooking dried beans, as it can keep them tough.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Soup
ingredients: 1 butternut squash (about 3 lb), peeled and cubed
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion and garlic 3 minutes.
Add squash, apple, broth and nutmeg.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Blend smooth, stir in coconut milk, season, and serve.
recipes.tip: The apple adds subtle sweetness that balances the savory squash.

recipes.title: Loaded Potato Soup
ingredients: 2.5 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Add potatoes, onion, garlic and broth to the pot.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Mash partially for a chunky-creamy texture.
Turn on Sauté, stir in milk and cheddar until melted.
Season and top each bowl with bacon and green onions.
recipes.tip: Leave some potato chunks unmashed for a heartier, restaurant-style texture.

recipes.title: White Chicken Chili
steps: Add chicken, beans, chiles, onion, garlic, cumin, oregano and broth to the pot.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 15 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Remove chicken, shred, and return to the pot.
Stir in sour cream, season, and serve.
recipes.tip: Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the chili naturally.

recipes.title: Moroccan Chickpea Stew
ingredients: 1 tbsp ras el hanout (or 1 tsp each cumin, cinnamon, paprika)
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion and garlic 3 minutes.
Stir in ras el hanout for 30 seconds.
Add chickpeas, tomatoes, broth and sweet potato.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 6 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Stir in spinach until wilted, season, and serve over couscous if desired.
recipes.tip: Ras el hanout is a one-jar shortcut to authentic North African flavor.

recipes.title: Thai Coconut Chicken Soup (Tom Kha Gai)
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced
steps: Add chicken, coconut milk, broth, ginger, lemongrass and mushrooms to the pot.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Remove ginger and lemongrass.
Stir in fish sauce and lime juice, top with cilantro and chili, and serve.
recipes.tip: Add the lime juice at the very end so its bright flavor stays fresh.

recipes.title: Vegetable Quinoa Soup
steps: Turn on Sauté, heat oil, and cook onion, carrots, celery and garlic 4 minutes.
Add quinoa, tomatoes, broth and herbs.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 2 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Stir in kale until wilted, season, and serve.
recipes.tip: Quinoa cooks fast under pressure; a natural release keeps it fluffy, not mushy.

recipes.title: Homemade Chicken Bone Broth
ingredients: Water to fill to 2/3 max line
steps: Add bones, vegetables, garlic, vinegar, bay leaf and peppercorns to the pot.
Pour in water up to the 2/3 max fill line.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 120 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally (full release).
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, discard solids, and cool.
recipes.tip: The splash of vinegar helps extract minerals from the bones for a richer broth.

recipes.title: Vegetable Broth
ingredients: Water to fill to 2/3 max line
steps: Add all vegetables, garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns and parsley to the pot.
Pour in water up to the 2/3 max fill line.
Seal lid and Pressure Cook on High for 30 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally (full release).
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, discard solids, and cool.
recipes.tip: Save vegetable scraps in the freezer all week, then make broth from them for free.

recipes.title: White Basmati Rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs clear; drain.
Add rice, water, salt and oil to the pot; stir once.
Pressure Cook (or Rice) on High for 4 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release remaining pressure.
Fluff with a fork and serve.
recipes.tip: A 1:1 water ratio plus natural release gives separate, non-mushy grains.

recipes.title: Brown Rice
steps: Rinse brown rice and drain well.
Add rice, water and salt to the pot; stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 22 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Fluff and serve.
recipes.tip: Use 1.25 cups water per cup of brown rice for tender but firm grains.

recipes.title: Fluffy Quinoa
steps: Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine mesh strainer to remove bitterness; drain.
Add quinoa, water and salt; stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 1 minute.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Fluff with a fork.
recipes.tip: Just 1 minute at pressure plus a natural release cooks quinoa perfectly fluffy.

recipes.title: Steel-Cut Oats
steps: Add oats, water and salt to the pot; stir.
Pressure Cook (or Porridge) on High for 4 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Stir in maple syrup and cinnamon; it thickens as it sits.
Serve with milk and fruit.
recipes.tip: A 3:1 water ratio gives creamy oats; add toppings after cooking to keep them from scorching.

recipes.title: Coconut Rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs clear; drain.
Add rice, water, coconut milk, salt and sugar; stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Fluff gently and serve.
recipes.tip: Replace part of the water with coconut milk (not all) to keep the liquid ratio right and avoid scorching.

recipes.title: Cilantro Lime Rice
steps: Rinse rice and drain.
Add rice, water, salt and oil; stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Fluff, then stir in lime juice and cilantro.
recipes.tip: Add lime juice and cilantro after cooking to keep the flavor bright and the herbs green.

recipes.title: Mexican Red Rice
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil 2 minutes using Sauté mode.
Stir in rice and cumin; toast 1 minute.
Add water, tomato sauce and salt; stir and scrape the bottom well.
Pressure Cook on High for 6 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release; fluff.
recipes.tip: Scrape the bottom clean after adding liquid so the tomato doesn't trigger a burn warning.

recipes.title: Jeera (Cumin) Rice
steps: Heat ghee on Sauté; add cumin seeds and bay leaf until fragrant and sizzling.
Add drained rice; stir to coat 30 seconds.
Add water and salt; stir and scrape the bottom.
Pressure Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release; fluff.
recipes.tip: Bloom the cumin seeds in hot ghee first for the signature aroma.

recipes.title: Mushroom Rice Pilaf
steps: Sauté onion, garlic and mushrooms in butter 3-4 minutes until they release liquid.
Stir in rice to coat.
Add broth, salt and pepper; scrape the bottom well.
Pressure Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release; fluff.
recipes.tip: Let mushrooms release their water during sauté so the rice doesn't turn out soggy.

recipes.title: Easy Parmesan Risotto
steps: Sauté onion in butter and oil 2-3 minutes.
Add arborio rice; toast 1-2 minutes stirring.
Add wine and cook off 1 minute; add broth and salt, scraping the bottom.
Pressure Cook on High for 6 minutes; quick release.
Stir in Parmesan vigorously until creamy; serve immediately.
recipes.tip: Quick release and stir in cheese right away to get the creamy risotto texture without endless stirring.

recipes.title: No-Soak Black Beans
steps: Rinse and sort beans for stones.
Add beans, water, bay leaf and onion to the pot (no salt yet).
Pressure Cook on High for 25 minutes.
Natural release 20 minutes, then quick release.
Drain to taste, discard bay leaf, stir in salt.
recipes.tip: Salt after cooking so the bean skins stay tender; no soaking required.

recipes.title: No-Soak Chickpeas
steps: Rinse and sort chickpeas.
Add chickpeas and water to the pot (no salt yet).
Pressure Cook on High for 45 minutes.
Natural release 20 minutes, then quick release.
Drain and stir in salt; use in hummus, curries or salads.
recipes.tip: For very soft chickpeas for hummus, add 5 extra minutes and 0.5 tsp baking soda to the cooking water.

recipes.title: No-Soak Pinto Beans
steps: Rinse and sort beans.
Add beans, water, onion and garlic (no salt yet).
Pressure Cook on High for 25 minutes.
Natural release 20 minutes, then quick release.
Stir in salt; mash for refried beans if desired.
recipes.tip: Reserve some cooking liquid to loosen mashed refried beans.

recipes.title: No-Soak Kidney Beans
ingredients: 1 lb dry red kidney beans (rinsed, sorted)
steps: Rinse and sort beans well.
Add beans, water and bay leaf (no salt yet).
Pressure Cook on High for 30 minutes.
Natural release 20 minutes, then quick release.
Drain, discard bay leaf, stir in salt.
recipes.tip: Always fully cook kidney beans to destroy natural lectins; pressure cooking does this reliably.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Dal (Tarka Dal)
steps: Add lentils, water, turmeric, tomato and salt to the pot.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes; natural release 10 minutes then quick release.
In a small pan heat ghee, add cumin seeds, garlic and chili powder (the tarka).
Pour the tarka over the dal and stir.
Serve with rice or flatbread.
recipes.tip: Red lentils need no soaking and break down into a creamy dal; finish with a sizzling tarka for flavor.

recipes.title: Toor Dal (Yellow Split Pigeon Pea)
steps: Add toor dal, water, turmeric and salt to the pot.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes; natural release 10 minutes then quick release.
Whisk dal smooth; add a little hot water if too thick.
Heat ghee, add cumin, garlic, red chili and hing for the tempering.
Pour tempering over dal, stir and serve.
recipes.tip: Whisk the cooked dal smooth before tempering for the classic restaurant-style texture.

recipes.title: Coconut Lentil Curry
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil 2-3 minutes; add curry powder and tomato paste, stir 1 minute.
Add lentils and water; scrape the bottom well.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes; natural release 10 minutes then quick release.
Stir in coconut milk and salt; simmer on Sauté 2 minutes to thicken.
Serve over rice.
recipes.tip: Add coconut milk after pressure cooking so it stays smooth and doesn't trigger a scorch warning.

recipes.title: Lemony Yellow Split Pea Soup
steps: Sauté onion and carrot in oil 3 minutes; add cumin and stir.
Add split peas and broth; scrape the bottom.
Pressure Cook on High for 15 minutes; natural release 15 minutes then quick release.
Stir in salt and lemon juice; blend partially for a creamier texture if desired.
Serve warm.
recipes.tip: Split peas need no soaking; the lemon at the end brightens the whole pot.

recipes.title: Salsa Chicken
steps: Add chicken to pot; sprinkle with cumin, chili powder and salt.
Pour salsa over top (do not stir into a thick paste at the bottom).
Pressure Cook on High for 10 minutes.
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Shred chicken in the pot and stir into the salsa.
recipes.tip: Use chunky salsa for more texture; stir in a little broth if it looks dry.

recipes.title: Shredded Chicken for Tacos
ingredients: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (fresh or frozen)
steps: Pour broth into pot; add chicken in a single layer.
Sprinkle taco seasoning over chicken.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes for fresh, 15 minutes for frozen.
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Shred with two forks; stir in lime juice and a few spoons of cooking liquid.
recipes.tip: For frozen, separate the breasts as much as possible before cooking for even results.

recipes.title: Whole Roast-Style Chicken
steps: Rub chicken with salt, paprika, pepper and garlic powder.
Sauté: brown chicken breast-side down in oil 4-5 minutes; remove.
Add broth and trivet; set chicken on trivet breast-side up.
Pressure Cook on High for 25 minutes (about 6 min per lb).
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release. Check 165F in thigh.
recipes.tip: Crisp the skin under a broiler for 3-4 minutes after cooking.

recipes.title: One-Pot Chicken and Rice
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in chunks
steps: Sauté onion in oil 2-3 minutes.
Add rice, broth, chicken, garlic powder and salt; stir to combine.
Pressure Cook on High for 10 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Fluff with a fork and rest 2 minutes.
recipes.tip: Keep rice submerged and avoid stirring after adding broth to prevent a burn warning.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
steps: Sauté onion in butter 3 minutes; add ginger-garlic paste and spices, cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato puree and salt; add chicken and coat.
Pressure Cook on High for 10 minutes.
Quick release.
Stir in cream; simmer on Sauté 2-3 minutes to thicken.
recipes.tip: Blend the sauce before adding cream for a silky restaurant-style texture.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Chicken
steps: Combine soy sauce, brown sugar, water, garlic and ginger in pot; add chicken.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release.
Set to Sauté; stir in cornstarch slurry and simmer 2-3 minutes to thicken.
Serve over rice with sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Use low-sodium soy sauce to control saltiness in the concentrated sauce.

recipes.title: Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
steps: Whisk honey, soy sauce, ketchup and garlic in pot; add thighs and coat.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release.
Sauté and stir in slurry; simmer 2-3 minutes until glossy.
Spoon sauce over chicken to serve.
recipes.tip: Doubles easily; keep cook time the same and just increase sauce.

recipes.title: BBQ Pulled Pork
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut in 3-4 chunks
steps: Rub pork with brown sugar, paprika and salt.
Sauté: brown pork chunks in oil on all sides; remove.
Add broth, scrape bottom, return pork.
Pressure Cook on High for 60 minutes (about 20 min per lb of chunks).
Natural release 15 minutes, then quick release; shred and toss with BBQ sauce.
recipes.tip: Drain most cooking liquid before adding BBQ sauce so it isn't watery.

recipes.title: Classic Pot Roast
steps: Season roast with salt and pepper; sear in oil on all sides (Sauté).
Add broth and onion soup mix; scrape bottom.
Pressure Cook on High for 60 minutes.
Quick release; add carrots and potatoes.
Pressure Cook on High for 10 more minutes; natural release 15 minutes then quick.
recipes.tip: Cut potatoes large so they don't turn to mush in the second cook.

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
ingredients: 1.5 lb flank or chuck steak, thinly sliced
steps: Combine beef, soy sauce, broth, sugar and garlic in pot.
Pressure Cook on High for 10 minutes.
Quick release.
Sauté; stir in slurry and simmer 2-3 minutes to thicken.
Fold in steamed broccoli just before serving.
recipes.tip: Cook broccoli separately and add at the end so it stays bright and crisp.

recipes.title: Korean-Style Beef (Bulgogi-Inspired)
steps: Combine beef, soy sauce, sugar, grated pear, garlic and sesame oil in pot.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes.
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Sauté; stir in slurry and simmer 2-3 minutes.
Serve over rice with green onions and sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Grated pear tenderizes the beef and adds natural sweetness.

recipes.title: Carnitas (Mexican Pulled Pork)
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut in chunks
steps: Add all ingredients to pot.
Pressure Cook on High for 60 minutes.
Natural release 15 minutes, then quick release.
Shred pork; spread on a sheet pan.
Broil 5 minutes for crispy edges; spoon over some juices.
recipes.tip: The orange juice and broil step give authentic crispy-yet-juicy carnitas.

recipes.title: Italian Meatballs in Marinara
steps: Add meatballs to pot.
Pour marinara and water over; sprinkle Italian seasoning.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release.
Stir gently; top with mozzarella and let melt with lid off.
recipes.tip: Serve over pasta, in subs, or on their own with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Sausage and Peppers
steps: Sauté sausages in oil until browned; remove.
Add broth and scrape bottom; add peppers, onion, tomatoes and seasoning.
Nestle sausages back on top.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release; slice sausage if desired and serve in rolls.
recipes.tip: Brown the sausages first for deeper flavor and better texture.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Mac and Cheese
steps: Add macaroni, water, salt and butter to pot (pasta just covered).
Pressure Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Quick release carefully in bursts.
Stir in milk, cream cheese, then cheddar a handful at a time.
Stir until creamy; rest 2 minutes to thicken.
recipes.tip: Pressure cook time = half the box's stovetop minutes, minus one.

recipes.title: One-Pot Spaghetti and Meat Sauce
steps: Sauté beef and onion until browned; drain excess fat.
Layer spaghetti in a crisscross pattern; pour water over to just cover.
Spoon marinara on top; do not stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Quick release; stir well and rest 2 minutes.
recipes.tip: Crisscrossing the broken pasta keeps it from clumping into a brick.

recipes.title: Penne with Sausage and Tomato
steps: Sauté sausage and garlic, breaking up meat, until browned.
Add penne and broth so pasta is just covered; stir once.
Pour marinara on top; do not stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 6 minutes.
Quick release; stir in parmesan until creamy.
recipes.tip: Penne cook time is roughly half the box time; 6 minutes suits most brands.

recipes.title: Lentil Bolognese
ingredients: 1.5 cups brown or green lentils, rinsed
steps: Sauté onion, carrot and garlic in oil 4-5 minutes.
Add lentils, tomatoes, broth, seasoning and salt; stir.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Stir and simmer on Sauté to thicken if needed; serve over pasta.
recipes.tip: A splash of balsamic or soy sauce at the end deepens the savory flavor.

recipes.title: Steamed Broccoli
ingredients: 1 large head broccoli, cut into florets
steps: Pour 1 cup water into the inner pot and place the trivet/steamer basket.
Add broccoli florets to the basket.
Lock lid, set Steam for 0 minutes (or 1 minute for softer florets).
Quick release immediately when the cycle ends.
Toss with oil/butter, salt and pepper.
recipes.tip: Quick release the instant it finishes—residual heat overcooks broccoli into mush.

recipes.title: Steamed Corn on the Cob
steps: Add 1 cup water and the trivet to the pot.
Stand or stack the corn on the trivet.
Steam for 2 minutes.
Quick release.
Slather with butter and salt.
recipes.tip: Cut ears in half if they don't fit; they'll stack neatly upright.

recipes.title: Steamed Asparagus
steps: Add 1 cup water and steamer basket to the pot.
Lay asparagus in the basket.
Steam for 1 minute (thin spears) or 2 minutes (thick).
Quick release immediately.
Drizzle with olive oil, squeeze lemon, season.
recipes.tip: Use 1 minute for pencil-thin asparagus to keep it bright and crisp-tender.

recipes.title: Perfect Hard-Boiled Eggs (5-5-5)
steps: Add 1 cup water and the trivet to the pot.
Place eggs on the trivet.
Pressure Cook (Manual) on Low for 5 minutes.
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release.
Transfer eggs to an ice bath for 5 minutes, then peel.
recipes.tip: The 5-5-5 (cook-natural-ice) gives firm yet tender eggs that peel cleanly; drop to 5-4-5 for jammy yolks.

recipes.title: Soft-Boiled Eggs
steps: Add 1 cup water and trivet to the pot.
Set eggs on the trivet.
Pressure Cook on Low for 3 minutes.
Quick release immediately.
Ice bath 2 minutes; peel gently and serve with toast soldiers.
recipes.tip: For runny-center soft eggs, do not natural release—quick release the moment the timer beeps.

recipes.title: Egg Bites
ingredients: 0.25 cup cooked bacon or diced ham
steps: Blend eggs, cottage cheese, cheddar, salt and pepper until smooth.
Grease a silicone egg-bite mold; sprinkle bacon/ham into each cup, then pour in egg mixture.
Cover mold with foil. Add 1 cup water and trivet to pot; set mold on trivet.
Pressure Cook on High for 8 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release; pop out the bites.
recipes.tip: Blending the cottage cheese in makes the bites silky like the coffee-shop version.

recipes.title: Steamed Baby Potatoes
steps: Add 1 cup water and steamer basket to the pot.
Add the baby potatoes.
Pressure Cook on High for 10 minutes (8 for very small).
Quick release.
Toss hot potatoes with butter, parsley and salt.
recipes.tip: Keep potatoes uniform (about 1.5 in.) so they cook evenly; halve larger ones.

recipes.title: Steamed Salmon
ingredients: Salt, pepper and dill to taste
steps: Add 1 cup water and trivet to the pot.
Season salmon; place skin-side down on foil or directly on the trivet, top with lemon slices.
Pressure Cook on Low for 3 minutes (thick fillets) or Steam 2 minutes for thin.
Quick release.
Check that it flakes; serve immediately.
recipes.tip: Low pressure for 3 minutes keeps salmon moist; add a minute only for fillets over 1.5 in. thick.

recipes.title: Steamed White Fish
steps: Add 1 cup water and trivet to the pot.
Place fish on a heatproof plate that fits inside; top with ginger and scallion.
Steam for 3 minutes.
Quick release.
Drizzle with soy sauce and serve over rice.
recipes.tip: A heatproof plate catches the flavorful juices instead of losing them to the water.

recipes.title: Steamed Shrimp
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Add 1 cup water and steamer basket to the pot.
Toss shrimp with Old Bay; place in basket.
Steam for 1 minute.
Quick release immediately.
Serve with lemon and cocktail sauce.
recipes.tip: Shrimp cook fast—quick release at once and pull them out so they stay snappy, not rubbery.

recipes.title: Steamed Dumplings (Frozen)
ingredients: 1 tsp sesame oil (to oil the basket)
Soy sauce + rice vinegar for dipping
steps: Add 1 cup water and a steamer basket lined with parchment or lightly oiled to the pot.
Arrange dumplings in a single layer, not touching.
Steam for 8 minutes (frozen) or 5 minutes (fresh).
Quick release.
Serve with dipping sauce.
recipes.tip: Oil the basket or use perforated parchment so the dumpling skins don't stick and tear.

recipes.title: Steamed Green Beans
steps: Add 1 cup water and steamer basket to the pot.
Add green beans.
Steam for 1 minute (crisp-tender) or 2 minutes (softer).
Quick release immediately.
Toss with butter and salt.
recipes.tip: Shock in ice water if serving cold for a salad—keeps them vivid green.

recipes.title: Steamed Artichokes
ingredients: Melted butter or aioli for dipping
steps: Add 1.5 cups water and trivet to the pot; squeeze in lemon and drop the halves in.
Set artichokes stem-up on the trivet.
Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes (large) or 9 minutes (small).
Quick release.
Check a leaf pulls easily; serve with melted butter.
recipes.tip: A leaf should slide out with a light tug when done—add 2-3 minutes for very large globes.

recipes.title: Steamed Cauliflower
steps: Add 1 cup water and steamer basket to the pot.
Add cauliflower florets.
Steam for 1 minute (firm) or 2 minutes (soft, mashable).
Quick release immediately.
Season and serve, or mash.
recipes.tip: Steam 2 minutes then mash with butter for a quick low-carb mashed-potato swap.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Mushrooms
steps: Set to Sauté (Normal/Medium) and melt butter.
Add mushrooms; cook 7-8 minutes, stirring, until browned and liquid evaporates.
Add garlic; sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with salt and pepper.
Turn off; stir in parsley and serve.
recipes.tip: Don't crowd or stir too early—let them sit to brown before the released water cooks off.

recipes.title: Caramelized Onions
steps: Set to Sauté (Less/Low) and heat butter and oil.
Add onions and salt; stir to coat.
Cook 25-30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deep golden.
Deglaze with a splash of water if they stick.
Stir in balsamic at the end; turn off.
recipes.tip: Use the Less sauté setting and be patient—rushing on high heat burns rather than caramelizes.

recipes.title: Quick Vegetable Stir-Fry
ingredients: 4 cups mixed veg (broccoli, pepper, carrot, snap peas)
steps: Set to Sauté (More/High) and heat the oil.
Add garlic and ginger; stir 30 seconds.
Add the harder veg (carrot, broccoli) first; cook 4 minutes.
Add quick-cooking veg (pepper, snap peas); cook 3 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce and sesame oil; toss 1 minute and turn off.
recipes.tip: Use the More setting for real stir-fry sear; add veg in order of density so nothing overcooks.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut in large chunks
steps: Rub pork with brown sugar, paprika and salt.
Add onion and broth to the pot; place pork on top.
Set Slow Cook on Low for 8 hours (or High 5 hours), lid on with vent set to Venting.
Shred pork with two forks; discard excess liquid.
Stir in BBQ sauce and serve on buns.
recipes.tip: Set the steam valve to Venting when slow cooking—sealed lids trap too much heat.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Beef Chili
steps: Use Sauté to brown the beef with onion and garlic; drain fat.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, tomatoes, beans and salt.
Switch to Slow Cook on Low for 6 hours (or High 3 hours), vent set to Venting.
Stir and adjust seasoning.
Serve with cheese and sour cream.
recipes.tip: Browning the beef on Sauté first builds far more flavor than dumping it in raw.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Applesauce
steps: Add apples, water, lemon juice and cinnamon to the pot.
Slow Cook on Low for 4 hours (or High 2 hours), vent Venting.
Stir; mash with a potato masher (or leave chunky).
Add sugar to taste if needed.
Cool and store refrigerated up to a week.
recipes.tip: A mix of sweet and tart apples gives the most balanced flavor—skip the sugar with sweet apples.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Chicken Tortilla Soup
steps: Add all ingredients to the pot and stir.
Slow Cook on Low for 6 hours (or High 3 hours), vent Venting.
Remove chicken and shred; return to pot.
Stir and adjust salt.
Top with tortilla strips, cheese, avocado and lime.
recipes.tip: This is a true dump-and-go—no browning needed; just stir and walk away.

recipes.title: Homemade Instant Pot Yogurt
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain yogurt with live active cultures (starter)
steps: Pour milk into the inner pot. Secure lid (vent position is fine; no pressure used).
Press Yogurt, then adjust to Boil. The pot heats milk to about 180F to denature proteins.
When the cycle ends, check temp; it should be ~180F. If short, use Sauté on Low to reach it, stirring.
Remove inner pot and cool milk to 110F (30-45 min). Speed it up in a cold-water bath.
Whisk the 2 tbsp starter into 1 cup of the warm milk, then stir back into the pot.
Return pot, secure lid, press Yogurt and set time to 8:00 hours. The display counts up.
When done, refrigerate at least 4 hours to set. For Greek-style, strain through cheesecloth.
recipes.tip: Cooler, longer incubation yields milder yogurt; 8-10 h gives a good tangy balance. Save 2 tbsp as next starter.

recipes.title: Creamy Rolled Oats
ingredients: 1.75 cups water (or 1 cup water + 0.75 cup milk)
steps: Add oats, liquid and salt to the inner pot; stir.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 3 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release the rest.
Stir in vanilla and any sweetener; serve.
recipes.tip: Do not use quick or instant oats here—they turn to mush. Rolled oats hold texture.

recipes.title: Breakfast Quinoa
steps: Rinse quinoa thoroughly to remove bitter saponins. Add all ingredients to the pot; stir.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 1 minute.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release remaining.
Fluff with a fork. Top with berries, nuts or extra milk.
recipes.tip: Rinsing is essential—unrinsed quinoa tastes soapy/bitter.

recipes.title: Crustless Egg Frittata
ingredients: 0.5 cup chopped cooked veggies (spinach, peppers, onion)
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Stir in cheese and veggies.
Grease a 7-inch baking dish; pour in the mixture. Cover loosely with foil.
Add 1.5 cups water to the pot; set trivet inside. Lower the dish on a foil sling.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 20 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release. Lift out, let stand 5 minutes, slice.
recipes.tip: Pre-cook watery veggies first so the frittata doesn't turn out runny.

recipes.title: Sausage & Hash Brown Casserole
ingredients: 2 cups frozen shredded hash browns, thawed
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Stir in hash browns, sausage and cheese.
Grease a 7-inch dish; add mixture. Cover loosely with foil.
Add water and trivet to the pot; lower dish on a foil sling.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 25 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
recipes.tip: Squeeze thawed hash browns dry in a towel to avoid a watery casserole.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Banana Bread
steps: Mix mashed bananas with melted butter. Stir in sugar, egg and vanilla.
Sprinkle baking soda and salt over the batter; mix. Fold in flour just until combined.
Pour into a greased 7-inch pan. Cover loosely with foil.
Add water and trivet to the pot; lower pan on a foil sling.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 55 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release. A toothpick should come out clean; cook 5-10 more minutes if wet. Cool before slicing.
recipes.tip: The riper (blacker) the bananas, the sweeter and more flavorful the loaf.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Cheesecake
steps: Mix crumbs and melted butter; press into a greased 7-inch springform pan. Freeze while mixing filling.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Add eggs one at a time on low speed. Mix in sour cream and vanilla.
Pour over crust. Tap pan to release bubbles. Cover with foil.
Add water and trivet to the pot; lower pan on a foil sling.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 35 minutes.
Let pressure release fully naturally (do not quick release—prevents cracking). Center should be slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temp, then refrigerate at least 6 hours before serving.
recipes.tip: Room-temperature cream cheese and eggs are critical for a smooth, lump-free batter.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Rice Pudding
ingredients: 1 cup arborio or short-grain white rice
steps: Add rice, water and salt to the pot; stir.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 12 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
In a bowl, whisk milk, sugar and egg yolks. Stir into the hot rice.
Press Sauté (Low) and cook, stirring constantly, 2-3 minutes until thickened. Do not boil hard.
Stir in vanilla and cinnamon. It thickens further as it cools.
recipes.tip: Tempering—whisk a little hot rice into the yolk mixture first—prevents scrambled eggs.

recipes.title: Quick Instant Pot Applesauce
steps: Add apples, water, lemon juice and cinnamon to the pot.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 5 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Mash with a potato masher for chunky, or blend for smooth. Stir in sugar if needed.
recipes.tip: A mix of sweet and tart apples gives the best balanced flavor; often no added sugar needed.

recipes.title: Dulce de Leche
ingredients: Water to cover the jars by 1 inch
steps: Pour condensed milk into a half-pint mason jar; cover loosely with the lid (finger-tight, not sealed).
Place trivet in the pot. Set jar on trivet. Add water to cover the jar by about 1 inch.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 35 minutes (lighter) up to 45 minutes (darker).
Let pressure release fully naturally.
Carefully remove the hot jar; let cool. Stir until smooth and creamy.
recipes.tip: Lids must be only loosely finger-tight—never fully sealed—so jars don't build dangerous pressure.

recipes.title: Poached Pears
ingredients: 4 firm pears (Bosc or Anjou), peeled, stems on
1.5 cups red wine or grape/pomegranate juice
steps: Add wine/juice, water, sugar, cinnamon and orange peel to the pot; stir to dissolve sugar.
Stand the peeled pears upright in the liquid.
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 3 minutes (firm-ripe) to 4 minutes (firmer).
Quick release. Remove pears gently.
Optional: Sauté the liquid 5-10 minutes to reduce into a syrup; spoon over pears.
recipes.tip: Use firm, slightly underripe pears—soft ones turn mushy under pressure.

recipes.title: Chocolate Lava Cakes
steps: Melt chocolate and butter together (microwave in short bursts); stir smooth.
Whisk in powdered sugar, then eggs and yolks, then flour and vanilla until just combined.
Divide among 4 greased ramekins. Cover each loosely with foil.
Add water and trivet to the pot; place ramekins on trivet (stagger if needed).
Secure lid, valve to Sealing. Pressure Cook on High for 9 minutes.
Quick release. Edges should be set, centers soft. Run a knife around and invert onto plates.
recipes.tip: The molten center depends on not overcooking—8-9 minutes is the sweet spot.
